what: When a project has a nodes: block, the sky's Roadmap lens lays stars out by dependency layer from the node graph instead of the stages table. The core works the layers out and sends them; the face only draws them.
expectations: A project with a nodes: block shows one column per dependency layer of its node graph, headed by its layer number; layer 0 is a node with no after.
A star joins the layer of the node named by its node:<id> label, and the order inside each column is the existing barycenter pass.

A star with no node (no node:<id> label, or a label naming an id not in the nodes: block) falls back to the stages layout and is still drawn: it goes in its stage's column after the layer columns, or in Unstaged when no stage holds it, so no star disappears.
A project without a nodes: block, or with an empty one, keeps the stages layout exactly as today, including the no-stages-table message.
The core sends Star.nodeLayer and Constellation.nodeLayers only when the project has a nodes: block; older sky answers stay valid.
